elaine: quick sync — I spun up a tiny run of a sparse-prefetch variant on ember-13b-4bit (on-node) to see end-to-end effects for speculative decode. short notes and numbers below.

micah: nice — what do you mean by sparse-prefetch? a smaller cache, or skipping tokens?

elaine: neither exactly. it's a prefetch that selectively loads KV rows for top-K predicted heads only (cheap heuristic) instead of the full attention window. idea: reduce mem bandwidth for quantized kernels.

raj: sounds promising. what config did you run? can you paste the minimal snippet?

elaine: ```
model: ember-13b-4bit-q
decode: speculative
spec-policy: two-tier
sparse-prefetch: true
prefetch-k: 12  # top-K attention rows to materialize
prefetch-window: 256
batching: continuous
quant-backend: int4-fused-kernel
```

micah: thanks. how does perf look vs baseline (regular prefetch / full KV)? numbers please.

elaine: very short run (1000 traces, mix of short/long):
- baseline (full prefetch, same HW): p50 tok-lat = 0.115s, p95 = 0.41s, tokens/sec = 210
- sparse-prefetch (K=12): p50 tok-lat = 0.082s, p95 = 0.33s, tokens/sec = 295
- tail: occasional spikes at ~0.9s when fallback path triggers (~1.8% of requests)

raj: solid p50 uplift (~28%) and throughput +40%. what about quality? any regressions on our eval sets?

elaine: ran three quick checks against onboard holdout: Evals: QA accuracy (closed-book), rougeL on summarization, and a synthetic toxic-safety probe.

- QA acc: baseline 78.3% -> sparse 77.6% (delta -0.7%)
- rougeL (short summarization set): baseline 41.2 -> sparse 40.9 (delta -0.3)
- safety probe: no new toxic tokens but slightly higher hallucination on abstractive prompts (observed in 14 cases out of 1k)

micah: small deltas, maybe within noise but worth tracking. do you suspect quantization + sparse prefetch interactions?

elaine: yeah. hypothesis: when KV rows are omitted we rely more on short-term cached prefixes; quantized kernels introduce rounding that amplifies small distribution shifts leading to rare token pivots. i attached some example decodes to the run: link -> https://internal/runs/1725667890 (mock link)

raj: can we do ablations: K=6, K=24, and an adaptive K (confidence-based) to see quality vs latency curve? also run longer batch of 10k traces.

elaine: plan:
- run K in {6,12,24} 10k traces each
- collect top-1 token divergence vs baseline, and per-prompt logp delta
- add an eval set of adversarial prompts (the hallucination holdout)
- instrument fallback counters (how often we materialize full window)

micah: add a rollout safety gate: if QA acc drops >1% we block canary. ops-bot, can you reserve a 4-GPU node for 3 hours tomorrow?

ops-bot: @micah node-4 reserved from 2024-03-12T13:00Z for 3h (tag: eng-ml-sparse-prefetch). :white_check_mark:

elaine: thanks. one more note — memory footprint dropped ~22% which could let us run a larger batch size on Dedicated (cost win). i'll capture cost estimate delta after ablations.

raj: nice. also toss in a simple perplexity delta and spike analysis for the fallback cases. if those fallback requests correspond to long-context QAs we might pattern-match and force full-prefetch for them.

micah: agreed. timeline?

elaine: start ablations tonight, short results by EOD tomorrow, full 10k over the weekend. i'll post a short summary and examples in this thread.

raj: thanks — and please flag any consistent failure modes early. :eyes: 

micah: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: run-171566: ablation jobs queued (ember-13b-4bit K6/K12/K24). ETA 2h.

elaine: will do.
